This relationship is supported by the evidence that Amoxapine, a related compound, binds to Orm1, suggesting a potential mechanism by which Desipramine may influence Orm1 through shared pharmacological pathways. The lowest common ancestor of Desipramine and Amoxapine is the Tricyclic Antidepressant class, indicating a common pharmacological profile, while the shared organic heterotricyclic compound suggests a structural similarity that may underpin their interactions. The integrated explanation highlights a possible dependency on Tricyclic Antidepressants and their associated compounds, positioning Orm1 as a target that could be affected by these drugs through binding mechanisms. The evidence supports a plausible, mechanistic link between Desipramine and Orm1, though further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction.
